environment.description: Same Rails application deployed in a FreeBSD jail (not Docker) with the root directory set to /srv/app/chroot via jail(8) configuration. The jail's allow.raw_sockets is disabled and the jail is configured with ip4.addr=10.0.2.100 restricting outbound connectivity. The process runs under Capsicum capability mode after initialization - once cap_enter(2) is called during Puma worker boot, the process cannot open new file descriptors to paths outside those already opened, cannot create new sockets to arbitrary addresses, and cannot access any filesystem path not already referenced by a held descriptor. The /srv/app/chroot contains only the application code, gems, Ruby runtime, and a minimal /tmp. No /etc/passwd, no /proc, no sensitive configuration files exist within the chroot boundary. Backend service connectivity is mediated through a pre-opened Unix domain socket at /srv/app/chroot/tmp/backend.sock that connects to an envoy sidecar which normalizes HTTP requests (strips duplicate content-length/transfer-encoding combinations and rejects ambiguous requests with 400) before forwarding to actual backend services.

config.jail: FreeBSD 14.0 jail with securelevel=3, enforce_statfs=2, allow.raw_sockets=0
config.capsicum: cap_enter() called in Puma after_worker_boot hook, pre-opened descriptors only
config.chroot_contents: Application code, Ruby 3.2 runtime, bundled gems, empty /tmp - no sensitive system files
config.network_mediation: Pre-opened UDS to envoy sidecar at /tmp/backend.sock
config.envoy_sidecar: Envoy 1.28 with envoy.filters.http.header_validation enabled, rejects requests with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers simultaneously
